text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government extended parliament's four-year mandate by eight months, and the mandate of municipal councils by one year. Last municipality election was held in 1963.
- The weekly treasury bill issue of April 17 raised 346.6 billion Lebanese pounds; the issue posted a nominal surplus of subscription against maturity of 82.6 billion pounds.
- Israeli shelling on wide areas in south Lebanon.
- Arab and International labour organisations will attend the elections of General Confederation of Labour's leadership on Thursday.
- Foreign Ministry continues contacts to evacuate Lebanese Nationals from Zaire.
- The five-nation group monitoring ceasefire in south Lebanon will discuss today an Israeli complaint after Hizbollah attacked a pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army militia car on Sunday.
- Ministry of Defence halts suspends weapons licences for one day during the CGTL elections on Thursday.
